drhp.expansion: The Company continued retail network expansion during the year, focused on Tier-II and Tier-III cities through Company-owned, franchised and distribution-led formats, taking its exclusive retail outlet network beyond 475-plus stores, alongside modernisation/renovation of select legacy stores. Separately, capital expenditure during the year was primarily directed towards moulds, machinery, furniture and fixtures and other business-related capital requirements, funded substantially through internal accruals with no specific term loan availed for capex.

- integration: in-house manufacturing capabilities and manufacturing network supporting productivity and cost competitiveness — evidence: Company continued to leverage its in-house manufacturing capabilities and manufacturing network to improve …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Continued pressure on input and raw material costs was cited as a primary driver of margin moderation despite revenue growth during FY26.
- Regular increases in minimum wages and consequent increase in employee benefit costs, including impact from the new Labour Codes, added to cost pressures and compressed margins.
- Operating and profitability performance was impacted by moderation in demand in certain quarters amid prevailing economic uncertainties.
- Trade receivables outstanding for more than 180 days was identified by the statutory auditors as a key audit matter requiring evaluation of recoverability.
- Pending matters relating to VAT, Service Tax, Labour and Income Tax/TDS before various judicial forums, with provisioning based on management's assessment of probability of the liability arising.
- Corporate Governance Report flags that global trade tensions and changes in tariff structures in major export markets remain important risks for the footwear industry, requiring market diversification and stronger supply chains.
- The GST rate cut on footwear was substantially aligned with passing the tax benefit to consumers, so it did not directly translate into a corresponding increase in the Company's profitability during the year.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Improve manufacturing and operational efficiencies, optimise product mix, exercise cost discipline and strengthen working capital management to improve margins.
- Pursue a calibrated and sustainable growth strategy focused on strengthening market position and improving operational and capital efficiency.
- Leverage GST rationalisation on footwear (up to Rs 2,500 per pair, 12% to 5% effective 22 September 2025) to strengthen value proposition and expand the addressable consumer base.
- Strengthen in-house manufacturing capabilities and process automation, sourcing optimisation and capacity …
